one_tool_many_jobs.description: Show one of our tools solving a chain of different small problems for one character, each beat adding a new use ('plus', 'bonus'). End with a before/after cost or time anchor.
one_tool_many_jobs.hook_pattern: This one [small thing] is perfect for [seasonal chore]

big_news_number.description: Open with a news-style announcement of one number or limit in a tool (for example a size in KB) on screen. Let the narrator show it removing the old problem for a character.
big_news_number.hook_pattern: Big news for [group]: [specific number] and no [annoying limit]

danger_zone_demo.description: Show the 'danger zone' of a task in 3D, such as a form being rejected, and then let the tool clear it. Narrate the two or three signals the character should watch for.
danger_zone_demo.hook_pattern: The most useful [thing] ever, because [danger or loss it prevents]

twist_one_twist_two.description: Show an ordinary-looking file or task. Narrate 'twist number one' and 'twist number two' as the tool's surprising abilities are revealed in turn.
twist_one_twist_two.hook_pattern: Throw away your boring [object], this one has [N] twists

regret_conversation.description: Have two 3D characters talk, where one says what they wish they had known about a document tool before a deadline. Narrate the regret line by line, then give the simple lesson.
regret_conversation.hook_pattern: A stranger's regret in one sentence, with big plain captions

two_vs_three_upgrade.description: Show that everyone does the job in two steps, but the tool does it in one. Use a counter on screen, and cut it before the story gets too long.
two_vs_three_upgrade.hook_pattern: Everyone does [two things], but you can do [three] at once

smallest_in_the_world_proof.description: Open by calling the file or tool the lightest, smallest or fastest of its kind. Have the narrator back it with two concrete numbers (KB, seconds or pages) shown on a panel, then close on a relatable payoff.
smallest_in_the_world_proof.hook_pattern: This is the smallest/most [adjective] [thing] in the world, and here is the proof in numbers

i_tested_n_so_you_dont_have_to.description: A narrator says they tried several ways of doing a document task, such as common apps or screenshots. A results panel shows most of them failing with errors or bad sizes, and the final panel shows one that works.
i_tested_n_so_you_dont_have_to.hook_pattern: I tested [N] [things] so you don't have to, and surprisingly none of them worked

poor_thing_mishap.description: A short, funny story where a file suffers a common mistake and the narrator pities it. A quick fix ends the scene.
poor_thing_mishap.hook_pattern: Poor [thing], look what people did to it

custom_unboxing_walkthrough.description: Narrator proudly shows a personalised result, such as a finished passport photo or a signed form, and walks through its details.
custom_unboxing_walkthrough.hook_pattern: This video is extra special because I have my own custom [thing]
